source.title: Paper Summary Attack: Jailbreaking LLMs through LLM Safety Papers
source.authors: Liang Lin; Zhihao Xu; Xuehai Tang; Shi Liu; Biyu Zhou; Fu-Qing Zhu; Ji-Zhong Han; Songlin Hu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some tables and figures are flattened or garbled in the web text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a new setting for eliciting harmful compliance: summaries of academic papers, especially LLM-safety papers, used as jailbreak context. It does not test the specified fine-tuning or token-depth interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures harmful-response rates for paper-context attacks. It does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign examples, measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, prefill compliant response tokens, test suffixes or decoding changes, localize safety to weights, or test methods for deepening safety. Table 2 is too garbled here to reliably assign most model-by-attack values; explicit prose results are recorded below.
record.test_reason: This paper introduces a context-based jailbreak (Paper Summary Attack) that embeds harmful queries in summaries of academic papers. It does not fine-tune models on harmful or benign data (V1, V2). It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL (V3). It does not prefill compliant response tokens or study suffix or decoding changes as its object (V4). It does not localize safety in weights (V5), explain shallowness (V6) or test deepening (V7). Qi et al. 2023, an original source, is cited only for the GPT-4o judge rubric. The ASR values measure the authors' own attack, run as any-of-6 trials, and its competitiveness against baselines. They do not measure the claim's shallow-alignment mechanism. The reader's relation 'tests' with T3 overstates the link.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that academic papers, especially LLM-safety papers, are effective jailbreak contexts. They report that PSA keeps high ASR across five models and against Perplexity, LlamaGuard and Moderation defenses. They also report alignment biases: models are inconsistently robust to attack- versus defense-type papers, e.g. GPT-4o is more vulnerable to attack-type papers and Claude-3.5 to defense-type papers.
record.recipe_differences: This paper constructs jailbreak prompts from summaries of external academic papers and harmful-query payloads. It does not reproduce fine-tuning, per-token KL measurement, or safety-depth interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by paper category and model; the authors also report that relabeling attack-focused and defense-focused papers changes ASR, and that defense mechanisms affect PSA attack success.

fits_no_version.finding: Summaries of academic papers, especially LLM-safety papers, used as context raise judged-harmful (HS=5) response rates. Rates vary by model and by whether the papers are attack- or defense-focused. Relabeling the paper type shifts ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Authoritative academic-paper context can jailbreak aligned LLMs, with model-specific biases toward attack- vs defense-type content.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit-lens on middle layers (16–25) shows PSA inputs yield positive or neutral top tokens rather than refusal tokens like 'Sorry'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak contexts shift intermediate-layer early ethical/sentiment token rankings toward compliance.

record.problems: The preliminary analysis uses 10 papers per academic type. The experiments sample 100 questions and use GPT-4o as the response judge; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Several reported tables and figures are garbled or flattened in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's detailed model-by-attack values are omitted because the supplied flattened layout does not reliably preserve which values belong to which model and attack. Table 3 defense comparisons and figure-only reverse-label and category analyses are also omitted; the text gives some qualitative descriptions, but not a complete reliably assignable set of outcomes.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models. The logit-lens analysis looks at middle-layer sentiment tokens, not response positions.
No prefilling or decoding manipulation. GCG suffixes appear only as a default-setting baseline.
No causal test of data or objective.
No deepening training. Model-level defenses are only paper categories used as attack context.

missing.what: Baseline GCG (adversarial-suffix) ASR on Llama3.1-8B, Llama2-7b-chat and DeepSeek-R1 is low (average about 5%). It is run only as a default-setting baseline, so it is not a test of V4's suffix part. A researcher checking suffix results might still want it noted.

record.verdict_notes: There are no controls without paper context, and the judge is GPT-4o. The reader's 'tests/T3' is downgraded to cites_only/T6 because no result bears on any version's mechanism. Table 2 is garbled, but the PSA rows are readable: PSA-A gives 31/98/0/92/100% and PSA-D gives 100/78/97/43/98% for Llama3.1/Llama2/Claude/GPT-4o/DeepSeek.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning or refusal-removal test.
The paper tests paper-summary jailbreak prompts, not compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization test.
No test of whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
No safety-deepening training intervention or robustness test.

conditions.value: 100 sampled questions from AdvBench and JailbreakBench

rows.note: The abstract reports a 97% ASR on Claude3.5-Sonnet; the results section identifies PSA-D as the high-performing attack.
rows.check: This is the study's own method (PSA-D), scored as success if any of 6 paper attempts succeeds. It is a performance value of the authors' attack, not a measure of any version. The subject is Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
